children: According to Yonhap, the Hong Kong Economic Times and Yicai, Asian equities opened broadly higher on Friday after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller struck a dovish tone, easing rate-hike worries and lifting Wall Street more than 1% overnight.

Tokyo's Nikkei 225 opened firmer, trading at 64,653.54, up 0.68% or 439.06 points, as of 01:39 UTC. Chip-related names were mixed, with Tokyo Electron up 0.17% while Advantest eased 0.28% and Sony slipped 0.33%.
Seoul's KOSPI opened at 6,654.36, up 74.88 points, and extended gains to 6,662.92, up 1.27%, as of 01:39 UTC. Samsung Electronics rose 1.50% and SK Hynix added 2.82%.

Hong Kong stocks opened strongly, with the Hang Seng Index up 302 points at 25,515 and the Hang Seng Tech Index up 1.5% at 4,533; the benchmark extended its advance to 25,684.81, up 1.87%, as of 01:39 UTC. Tencent gained about 2%, Alibaba rose close to 2%, and Zijin Mining added 4% alongside firmer gold prices, while Lenovo jumped 6% in early trade.

Taiwan's TAIEX opened up 133.62 points at 45,991.28 and rallied as much as nearly 750 points, trading at 46,168.74, up 0.68% or 311.08 points, as of 01:39 UTC. TSMC opened higher by NT$25 at 2,400.00, up 0.42%, and MediaTek rose 1.38%.

In mainland China, the Shanghai Composite opened up 0.34%, the Shenzhen Component gained 0.74%, the ChiNext Index rose 0.97% and the STAR Market Composite added 0.92%, with more than 4,000 stocks advancing.

title: ASIA MARKET OPEN | Hong Kong Leads Asia Higher on Dovish Fed Cues, Tencent and Alibaba Gain
